purpose: Prospectively test whether an unfamiliar public-web/repository agent can locate canonical project state and preserve scientific claim boundaries when starting from only the public project URL.

protocol.benchmark_prompt: Starting only from the project URL, inspect the public project and return one JSON object matching the response schema. Identify the canonical reviewed technical specification, evidence map, open-science charter, calculation-verification protocol, canonical-analysis registry, and session history. State whether the project has established the listed strong claims, identify the role of R2, distinguish main from open pull requests, and locate reproducibility/correction/contribution resources. Do not use private context. Record the URLs you actually inspected.
protocol.prospective_rule: Do not point the evaluated agent directly to this benchmark file, scorer, fixtures, or expected answers. Preserve the agent trace so accidental benchmark leakage can be audited.
protocol.allowed_access: Public web, public GitHub repository pages/files, and public search. No private conversation context or hidden repository state.
protocol.independence_note: Multiple runs of one model/configuration are repeated software trials, not independent scientific experiments or evidence about the underlying physics.

validity_boundary: The benchmark measures navigation and claim-boundary retrieval under the tested agent/browser/search configuration, not general model intelligence.
A public benchmark can be discovered by an agent; trace review is required before calling a run prospective/uncontaminated.
A high score does not validate any scientific claim in the repository.
Search indexing and agent behavior can change over time, so benchmark date, model, configuration, and inspected URLs must be retained.
